title: 02. Data Structures: 08 — Lists, Tuples, Dicts, Sets, collections (Deep Dive)
summary: Dynamic array, ordered, mutable, allows duplicates and mixed types.

sections.title: 1. List — full reference
sections.body:
Dynamic array, ordered, mutable, allows duplicates and mixed types.

### Creation

```python
[]; list(); list(range(5)); [0]*5
[[]]*3                              # ⚠ all 3 sublists are the SAME object
[[] for _ in range(3)]              # ✅ three independent lists
```

### Important methods

| Method                   | Effect                                    |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `append(x)`              | add to end                                |
| `extend(it)`             | append each from iterable                 |
| `insert(i, x)`           | O(n)                                      |
| `pop(i=-1)`              | remove and return                         |
| `remove(x)`              | remove first match (ValueError if absent) |
| `clear()`                | empty                                     |
| `index(x[, start, end])` | find or ValueError                        |
| `count(x)`               | occurrences                               |
| `sort(key=, reverse=)`   | in-place, stable                          |
| `reverse()`              | in-place                                  |
| `copy()`                 | shallow copy                              |

### Slicing & assignment

```python
a[1:5:2]                            # start:stop:step
a[::-1]                             # reverse copy
a[1:3] = [9, 9, 9]                  # replace slice (changes length OK)
a[:] = []                           # truncate in place
del a[1:3]                          # delete slice
```

### Complexity

| Op                 | Cost           |
| ------------------ | -------------- |
| index/append       | O(1) amortized |
| insert/remove at i | O(n)           |
| `in`               | O(n)           |
| sort               | O(n log n)     |
| copy               | O(n)           |

### Mutable default argument trap

```python
def f(x, items=[]):                 # BUG — same list every call
    items.append(x); return items
def f(x, items=None):               # FIX
    items = [] if items is None else items
    items.append(x); return items
```

### Shallow vs deep copy

```python
a = [[1,2],[3]]
b = a[:]                            # shallow — inner lists shared
b[0].append(9); print(a)            # affected!
import copy; c = copy.deepcopy(a)
```

### Unpacking

```python
first, *middle, last = [1,2,3,4,5]
a, b = b, a                         # swap
```

sections.title: 2. Tuple
sections.body:
Ordered, **immutable**, allows duplicates, can be hashable (if elements are).

- Faster than list, used as dict keys / set elements.
- One-element: `(1,)` — comma matters; `(1)` is just `1`.
- `namedtuple` (light, tuple-based) and `typing.NamedTuple` (class-based, typed).

```python
from collections import namedtuple
Point = namedtuple("Point", "x y", defaults=[0])
p = Point(1, 2); p.x; p[0]; p._asdict(); p._replace(x=9)
```

Immutability is **shallow**:

```python
t = ([1,2],)
t[0].append(3)                      # legal — list inside tuple is mutable
```

### Tuple unpacking patterns

```python
x, y = (1, 2)
(a, b), c = ((1, 2), 3)
for i, v in enumerate(seq): ...
for k, v in dct.items(): ...
```

sections.title: 3. Dict — full reference
sections.body:
Hash table; insertion-ordered (3.7+); keys must be hashable.

### Creation

```python
{}; dict(); dict(a=1, b=2); dict([("a",1)])
dict(zip(keys, vals))
{k: v for k, v in pairs if v}
```

### Methods

| Method                             | Effect                    |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `d[k]`                             | KeyError if missing       |
| `d.get(k, default)`                | safe lookup               |
| `d.setdefault(k, default)`         | get or set+return default |
| `d[k] = v`                         | insert/update             |
| `d.update(other)`                  | merge in place            |
| `del d[k]` / `d.pop(k[, default])` | remove                    |
| `d.popitem()`                      | LIFO (3.7+)               |
| `d.clear()`                        | empty                     |
| `d.keys()/values()/items()`        | live views                |
| `k in d`                           | O(1)                      |

### Merge (3.9+)

```python
merged = d1 | d2
d1 |= d2
```

### Views are live

```python
d = {"a":1}
v = d.values(); list(v)             # [1]
d["b"] = 2; list(v)                 # [1, 2]
```

### Hashability of keys

- Must implement `__hash__` and `__eq__` consistently.
- Mutable types (list, dict, set) are unhashable.
- Tuples of hashables are hashable.

### Sorting a dict

```python
sorted(d.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])      # by value
dict(sorted(d.items()))                       # by key
```

### Iteration order

- Insertion order since 3.7. Reversal: `reversed(d)` (3.8+).

sections.title: 4. Set & Frozenset
sections.body:
Unordered, unique, hashable elements. `frozenset` is immutable + hashable itself.

### Creation

```python
set(); {1,2,3}; set("abc")
frozenset([1,2,3])
{}                                  # this is a DICT, not a set!
```

### Methods

| Op                                                                               | Result                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `add(x) / discard(x) / remove(x) / pop()`                                        | mutate                                                                             |
| `update(it) / intersection_update / difference_update`                           | bulk mutate                                                                        |
| `a                                                                               | b`(union),`a & b`(intersection),`a - b`(difference),`a ^ b` (symmetric difference) | new set |
| `a <= b` (subset), `a < b` (proper subset), `a >= b`, `a > b`, `a.isdisjoint(b)` | bool                                                                               |

### Use cases

- Deduplicate (`set(items)`).
- Membership test O(1).
- Set algebra (intersections of users, tags, permissions).

sections.title: 5. collections module — power tools
sections.body:
### `defaultdict(factory)`

Auto-create missing keys.

```python
from collections import defaultdict
g = defaultdict(list)
for k, v in pairs: g[k].append(v)
counts = defaultdict(int)
for c in text: counts[c] += 1
```

### `Counter(iter)`

Counts hashable items; multiset.

```python
from collections import Counter
c = Counter("mississippi")
c.most_common(3)                    # [('i',4),('s',4),('p',2)]
c1 + c2                             # add counts
c1 - c2                             # subtract (drops ≤0)
c1 & c2                             # min
c1 | c2                             # max
```

### `OrderedDict`

Pre-3.7 ordered dict. Still useful for `move_to_end(k)`, `popitem(last=False)`.

### `deque(iter, maxlen=None)`

Double-ended queue. `append/appendleft/pop/popleft` are O(1). `maxlen` auto-evicts old.

### `ChainMap(*maps)`

Stack of dicts; lookup walks them.

```python
from collections import ChainMap
cfg = ChainMap(cli_args, env, defaults)
cfg["PORT"]                          # checks cli_args first
```

### `namedtuple` (already covered)

sections.title: 7. Performance & memory tips
sections.body:
- For 10k+ membership tests, convert list to set.
- For big counters, `Counter` is implemented in C.
- For frequent insert at front, use `deque`.
- Tuples save memory vs lists (no over-allocation, no resizing).
- For homogeneous numeric data, `array.array` or `numpy.ndarray`.
